content.text:
Here are some **notable art / artist-led collaborations from 2023**, especially in fashion, design, culture, and museums:

1. **Louis Vuitton × Yayoi Kusama**  
   A major luxury-art collaboration featuring Kusama’s signature polka dots across Louis Vuitton bags, shoes, accessories, perfumes, and immersive store/window installations. It was one of the most visible art-brand collabs of 2023. ([us.fashionnetwork.com](https://us.fashionnetwork.com/news/The-most-anticipated-fashion-collabs-of-2023%2C1472937.html?utm_source=openai))

2. **Mugler × H&M**  
   A high-profile fashion collaboration launched in May 2023, bringing Mugler’s sculptural, body-conscious aesthetic to a mass-market audience. ([nationalworld.com](https://www.nationalworld.com/lifestyle/fashion/a-look-back-at-the-biggest-fashion-collaborations-of-2023-4445751?utm_source=openai))

3. **Masquespacio × Monoprix**  
   Spanish design studio Masquespacio collaborated with French retailer Monoprix on a colorful summer collection of clothing, tableware, and home accessories inspired by 1980s pop aesthetics. ([usaartnews.com](https://usaartnews.com/news/artistic-collaborations-2023?utm_source=openai))

4. **Brooklyn Museum × Dior × Mickalene Thomas**  
   The 2023 Brooklyn Artists Ball, presented by Dior, featured a special collaboration with artist Mickalene Thomas and honored Carrie Mae Weems. ([thecitylife.org](https://thecitylife.org/2023/03/01/brooklyn-museum-to-honor-carrie-mae-weems-at-2023-brooklyn-artists-ball-made-possible-by-dior/?utm_source=openai))

5. **The Culture: Hip Hop and Contemporary Art in the 21st Century**  
   A major collaborative museum exhibition co-organized by the Baltimore Museum of Art and Saint Louis Art Museum. It connected contemporary art, music, fashion, and hip-hop culture, with artists such as Mark Bradford, Julie Mehretu, Tschabalala Self, Hank Willis Thomas, Carrie Mae Weems, and others. ([artbma.org](https://artbma.org/press-release/bma-to-open-groundbreaking-exhibition-on-the-impact-of-hip-hop-on-contemporary-art-and-material-culture-in-april-2023/?utm_source=openai))

6. **PhotoVogue Festival 2023 × AI / tech partners**  
   The 2023 PhotoVogue Festival explored image-making in the age of artificial intelligence, combining photography, AI, fashion, and technology through exhibitions and symposium programming. ([vogue.com](https://www.vogue.com/article/inside-the-photovogue-festival-2023?utm_source=openai))

7. **Helsinki Biennial 2023 × AI art curation project**  
   Researchers and artists developed an AI-curation project that reimagined Helsinki’s urban space using museum collections, machine perception, and synthetic 360-degree panoramas. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03753?utm_source=openai))

8. **Art Basel Miami Beach 2023 × luxury/fashion brand activations**  
   Art Basel Miami Beach continued to be a hub for collaborations between galleries, artists, luxury brands, fashion houses, and cultural institutions, with numerous brand activations surrounding the fair. ([vanityfair.com](https://www.vanityfair.com/style/2023/11/art-basel-miami-beach-2023-preview?utm_source=openai))

9. **Generative AI × artists / prompt-art communities**  
   2023 saw rapid growth in collaborations between artists and generative AI tools. Research from that year documented how prompt-based image-making became a developing creative practice, with prompts and outputs treated together as artistic work. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12253?utm_source=openai))

10. **Hip-hop 50th anniversary art collaborations**  
   Because 2023 marked 50 years of hip-hop, many exhibitions and cultural programs brought together visual artists, designers, musicians, photographers, and museums to frame hip-hop as a major contemporary art movement. The BMA/Saint Louis exhibition was one of the clearest examples. ([artbma.org](https://artbma.org/press-release/bma-to-open-groundbreaking-exhibition-on-the-impact-of-hip-hop-on-contemporary-art-and-material-culture-in-april-2023/?utm_source=openai))

If you mean **artist × brand collaborations specifically**, the biggest names from 2023 were probably **Louis Vuitton × Yayoi Kusama**, **Mugler × H&M**, and **Masquespacio × Monoprix**.
